findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee use gloved hands to pick up sliced bread from the floor and proceed to handle ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. The activity was ceased and corrected. The employee was instructed to wash hands and change gloves to correct the violation. Ensure that gloves are changed after tasks are interrupted. Also ensure that hands are being washed when changing gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- on the floor underneath the shelf of the walk in freezer (accumulated food debris)
- shelves of the stacked cooler near the dish area (dried food debris)
- floors underneath triple sink and behind grease collection station (accumulated food debris)
Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as often to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
PIC was unable to produce Food Handler certificates for employees during today’s inspection. Employees should obtain their Food Handler’s Certificate within 30 days of hire, and renew their certificates every 3 years. Ensure all employees complete food handler’s certificate training, and retain records on file for verification during inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a significant amount of syrup and biofilm accumulated around the multi-drink nozzles at both the server station and the drive thru. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the outer portion of the nozzles to be cleaned and wiped with a sanitizer cloth. Due to the affixed nature of the nozzles, inspector recommends brushing the multi-drink nozzles with a cleaning and sanitizing solution nightly. Food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the strawberries in the drive thru cold holding well to be out of temperature. Strawberries had an ambient temperature of 50F, and probed at 47F. Their sticker time indicated they had been on an ice bath for 6+ hours. CORRECTED- the PIC voluntarily discarded the strawberries. Ensure TCS foods are cold held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens. Out of temperature items must be used or discarded within 4 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 2 wet sanitizer cloths to be on the counter at the drive thru, as well as at the ice cream station’s triple sink. CORRECTED- PIC moved sanitizing cloths to sanitizer buckets. Wet textiles can allow for the growth and harborage of mold and other microorganisms. Ensure wet sanitizing cloths are stored in a sanitizer solution in between uses.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
1) Inspector observed a significant amount of grease and food debris on the baffles and fire suppression systems of the hood vents above the fryers. Grease drips pose a threat on contamination on RTE foods, and also pose a fire hazard to the facility. Steam Power cleans the facility’s hood vent system quarterly. PIC stated the baffles are cleaned on a weekly basis.
2) The racks in standing “fryer cooking” cooler contain grease accumulation and rust. Paint/ seal, or replace the nonfood contacts surfaces by next routine inspection.
Ensure nonfood contacts surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: PIC was unable to produce Food Handler certificates for employees during today’s inspection. Employees should obtain their Food Handler’s Certificate within 30 days of hire, and renew their certificates every 3 years. Ensure all employees complete food handler’s certificate training, and retain records on file for verification during inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
Signed employee reporting agreements were not available. PIC could not provide proof that employees are informed in a verifiable manner of foodborne illnesses and symptoms that would require them to be excluded from work in the kitchen. Facility has a blank reporting agreement that can be laminated and reviewed and signed by employees. Keep signed reporting agreements on file for all employees.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 2nd REPEAT: The side of front ice machine was observed to be soiled (moisture and green slime). Clean the exterior of the ice machine regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash, and general debris. [C]

findings.comment:

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not dispensing upon initial check of the dispenser in the men’s restroom. GM opened the dispenser to check batteries and troubleshoot. Paper towels dispensed properly after GM wiped the sensor and adjusted a switch.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11 Facility is Class II medium risk and is operating as a Class I high risk. While discussing practices at the close of daily operations, GM stated leftover portions of chili are cooled on an ice bath to be used again the next day. GM indicated this has always been the practice and was informed an upgrade to Class I is required to continue cooling and reheating chili. GM stated the practice would cease as of today and moving forward chili would not be cooled at the close of business.
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with the law

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dishes were observed sitting in sanitizer solution of 0ppm chlorine in the front 3 part sink. Employee working in the area stated the solution was from earlier and needed to be refreshed. Dishes were placed through ware washing cycle again and sanitized in a fresh solution observed at 100ppm. 
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed on the metal ledge by the door inside the left ice machine bin. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components [ice makers] shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Squeeze pouch of whipped topping stored in a container in the top holding area of the dessert topping cooler had surface temperatures ranging from 64F for the portion that was sticking out of the container to 41F-43F for the portion down inside the container.  GM moved the product to the bottom holding area to chill and store product. Best practices for storage were discussed. GM stated moving forward staff would be trained to remove product from the bottom cold holding area as needed and immediately place whipped topping back in the bottom after use. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Stack of cheese slices had surface temperatures of 58F-60F at the top and near 40F in the bottom where container was in direct contact with ice. Cheese slices were stacked to the top of the container where ice was not maintained. Best practices of smaller portions and addition of ice throughout the day were discussed. A portion of the cheese slices were wrapped and placed back in cold holding, and the ice bath was refreshed. Ensure enough ice is maintained to adequately surround containers on the bottom and all sides as far up on the outside as the depth of product inside the container. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop holder was starting to show signs of wear with rust forming in the crevice where scoop rests. Ice bag was used to provide a temporary liner. GM stated a new holder would be purchased. A clean container may also be used for scoop storage until a new side mounted holder is provided. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Right ice machine is currently off and empty to allow for cleaning. A gap was observed where the seal has worn away on the top left side between the ice maker and the bin. Light was visible on the inside of the bin where the gap was observed, which indicates the potential for debris to get in the ice bin. Provide proper repairs to seal the gap in question. In the meantime, cover the gap with material that is easy to maintain and/or switch out as needed (clean ice bags changed weekly, etc.) to protect ice if the machine is put back in use before repairs are done. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following items were observed to be soiled:
1. Bottom inside upright reach-in cooler at cook line (food debris);
2. Top of lower door on upright reach-in freezer at cook line (crumbs); and
3. Side of left ice machine adjacent to scoop storage (general buildup - from moisture/rust).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash, and general debris.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-202.14  Women's room door was not shutting properly. When closed it did not seal to be flush with the door frame. Repair the door so it shuts and seals properly.
All toilet rooms located within a food establishment must be enclosed with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

6-501.11 1 Handsink in women's room was not properly sealed to the wall. Recaulk the sink to the wall in the women's room.
2. Base coving was missing at the corner between the drive thru door and the cook line. GM noted they are in the process of getting estimates for repairs.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1. Floor was observed to be soiled with general buildup and debris in the following areas:
A. Under soda and slush machines in front service area;
B. Under left ice machine; and
C. Under front 3 part sink - floor drains with mold buildup.

2. Wall and base coving at mopsink were soiled with general buildup of splash and what appeared to possibly by mold.
Cleaning frequency was discussed for physical facilities.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-3401.11 Employee was observed having bare hand contact with breakfast sandwiches when preparing orders. Employee was observed washing hands prior to making food but was advised gloves or another suitable barrier is required when handling ready to eat foods. Employee stated they understood and was later observed wearing gloves when handling ready to eat foods.  
Except when washing fruits and vegetables or when ingredients will be added to food that is being fully cooked/has a kill step for pathogens, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Surfaces in both ice machines were soiled with varying degrees of mold accumulation. Ice machine on the left had mold buildup along the metal ledge behind the door hinge, and condensation was dripping off the mold into the ice. Both ice machines had mold on the inner surfaces of doors and on the walls. The right ice machine also had mold buildup on the baffle. Both ice machines were turned off and emptied during the inspection to allow for cleaning and sanitization in the machines. Significant progress was made to remove buildup prior to the conclusion of inspection. Ensure the ice machines are getting cleaned and sanitized as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Nozzle to bulk ketchup dispenser was observed with ketchup buildup. Manager stated the nozzle is cleaned every 3 to 4 days when the product is restocked. Manager was advised the nozzle should be cleaned daily/as needed to eliminate buildup. A full cleaning and sanitization of the nozzle should occur prior to restocking the dispenser. Nozzle was cleaned during the inspection.
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Hard ice cream mix was observed with surface and internal temperatures of 50F and 47.5F respectively in the bottom cold holding area. Temperature in the holding area was 50F. Product was assumed to have been stocked the evening prior. No orders for hard ice cream were prepared yet for the current operating day. Mix was discarded. Ice cream machine was turned off and will not be used until it is repaired and working properly. Manager will check the error message on the display and call for service if troubleshooting on-site cannot repair the issue. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle in chemical storage area containing yellow liquid was observed without a label. Product was confirmed by manager to be peroxide cleaner disinfectant and placed in properly labeled bottle. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 A portion of dirty mop water was observed in a mop bucket next to the mopsink. Manager finished disposing of the dirty mop water via the mopsink. Ensure dirty mop water is properly disposed of in the mop sink after use. 
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave it sitting in the facility as it can serve as a water source for pests.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-202.14  Women's room door was not shutting properly. When closed it did not seal to be flush with the door frame. Repair the door so it shuts and seals properly.
All toilet rooms located within a food establishment must be enclosed with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Wall above the large 3 part sink was damaged and had a couple holes in it. Repair the damaged areas above the large 3 part sink in back of the facility.
--Baseboard was pulling away from the wall by the mopsink behind the chemical storage shelving. Reseal the baseboard to the wall. 
--Handsink in women's room was not properly sealed to the wall. Recaulk the sink to the wall in the women's room.
--Ponding water was observed on the floor between the two floor drains under the small 3 part sink up front. Source of water was unknown but thought to possibly be from a couple condensate lines that were previously not positioned over one of the drains. Clean the floor and minimize ponding water to help reduce issues with worn grout. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Grease accumulation needs to be cleaned from the side of the fryer and the freezer next to the fryer where the skimmer is stored. Manager noted this area needs to be detailed and put on a routine cleaning schedule.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash, and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Flooring and baseboard remain to be repaired behind the used grease storage bin. Manger discussed plans for repairs (see general comments for details).
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee took a drink from a personal beverage and then began to put on gloves without handwashing in between. Employee just washed hands prior to getting a drink but was advised handwashing was required again prior to putting on gloves because of personal beverage consumption. Employee washed her hands again prior to putting on gloves to help with prep.
--Employee working the drive thru window was handling money and put on gloves to make beverages without handwashing in between. Employee was advised on handwashing prior to putting on gloves and working with food and single service articles. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after eating/drinking, prior to putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Surfaces in the ice machine were soiled with varying degrees of mold accumulation on the plastic baffle, the walls, and around the openings in the ceiling where ice drops from the ice maker. Ice was in contact with the mold on the baffle. The plastic baffle was wiped down with sanitizer during inspection, and ice was removed for discard. All surfaces inside the ice machine will be cleaned and sanitized at the close of business today. Ice machine will be checked again when inspector returns to check on pest control (11/12/19). 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Diffusers of soda machines were soiled with varying amounts of buildup. Ensure diffusers that cannot be removed from the machines getting manually washed, rinsed, and sanitized in place. 
--Inside ice machine was soiled with mold buildup (see #15 for additional information).
In equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed compartments, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Squeeze pouch of whipped topping was observed in a styrofoam cup within a container in the top holding area of the dessert topping cooler. Surface and internal temperatures were observed at 48F and 49F-50F respectively. Product was discarded. The styrofoam cup was likely acting as an insulator and causing the whipped topping to be above 41F because the temperature down inside the container was 39F. Consider storing the whipped topping in the bottom of the cooler and/or cease the practice of stacking a cup within the container. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 A dozen plus fruit flies were observed under and around the dirty dish area and around the floor drain by the used grease bin. Manager noted treatment has been ongoing, and facility was working with PCO to eliminate flies. PCO provided a product for cleaning and treatment that was currently in use and observed on the floor behind the used grease bin and in the drain adjacent to the grease bin. Management was advised on cleaning and repairs also needed in the area to help minimize potential food/water sources (see #55 for details)
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Metal ice scoop was stored on top of a soda syrup box by the ice machine. Manager removed the scoop and took it to 3 part sink for ware washing. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Employee working at drive thru prepared drinks and handled money with gloved hands. Gloves were eventually discarded. Proper use of gloves was discussed. Management was advised to reiterate proper glove use with all staff.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves (mold/food debris);
B) side of fryer next to freezer storage where skimmer is stored (grease buildup);  and
C) side of fryer next to fryers (grease splash).
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Ponding water and debris were observed around the pipes on the left side under the small 3pt sink up front and around the floor drain directly in front of the pipes. Clean the area and re-seal low lying areas to eliminate ponding water.
--Floor drain by used grease storage bin was soiled down inside with grimy, moldy buildup. The cover to the drain also had buildup on the underside. Clean down inside the drain and the cover. 
--Floor tiles had low grout and baseboard was loose behind the used grease storage bin. Ponding water and debris accumulation was observed. Manager also noted he was in the process of treating for flies in the area, so a greenish colored liquid was also present. Clean and repair this area to eliminate ponding water and debris accumulation. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Squeeze pouch of whipped topping in the top holding area of the dessert topping cooler was observed sticking up out of the container. Surface temperature was observed at 47°F-64°F, and internal temperature was 51°F-60°F. Manager stated no shakes were made yet for the current operating day, and the product was probably placed in there the evening prior. Labeling on the pouch says "keep refrigerated". Whipped topping was discarded.

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display, and service. 
Manager was advised on the option of time control for in-use pouches of whipped topping.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Mold buildup was observed inside the left ice machine around the opening in the ceiling where ice comes out. Manager immediately cleaned and sanitized the area of concern. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machines as frequently as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 

Food thermometer probe was observed with stuck on food debris. Probe was last used for morning temperature checks. Probe was wiped down with sanitizer solution. Sanitizing between uses and proper manual ware washing
up to very 4hrs after continuous use were discussed with manager.

Clean tongs hanging from shelving above the 3 part sink were observed to have water splash on them from general use of the faucet. Mold buildup was on the wall and general surfaces adjacent to where tongs were stored. One pair of tongs had what appeared to be stuck on grease/food debris. Manager cleaned and sanitized all the tongs during the inspection. Clean utensils need to be stored in a different location to avoid being exposed to splash from general use at the 3 part sink.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.160 - Cook was observed touching general surfaces with gloved hands, including but not limited handles of coolers and buttons on fryers, and continued food handling without changing gloves. Cook was advised on proper glove use and frequent glove changes, especially after touching general surfaces and before handling ready to eat foods.

Gloves are intended for one use and must be changed when soiled, torn, or an interruption in task occurs.
findings.citation_text:
750.512 - Employee was observed with a cell phone out on the back table where single service items (mints, ketchup packets, etc.) were being pre-stocked in paper bags. Employee did not wash hands between touching the cell phone and continuing to handle single service items. Handwashing was discussed with employee, and hands were washed prior to continuing the current task.
NOTE: Cell phones are filthy and hands should always be washed immediately after handling cell phones and prior to doing anything else in the facility. 

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and single service items.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-bucket solutions on cook line were observed at ~100-150ppm quat. Required concentration for company standards is 200ppm. All sani-bucket solutions were switched out with fresh solution (200ppm).

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) walkin cooler shelves (mold/food debris);   and
B) bottom inside reach-in cooler (food debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Leak was observed at the front 3 part sink. Water continues to run from the faucet even when both handles are in the off position. Repair the front 3 part sink.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1200 - Ponding water and debris were observed around the pipes on the left side under the small 3pt sink up front and around the floor drain directly in front of the pipes. Clean the area and make effort to keep it dry.
Make repairs to the floors throughout where needed, and minimize ponding water.

All floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Walls were observed with mold buildup in the walkin cooler and above the backsplash of the 3 part sink. Clean the walls as daily/needed to eliminate buildup of mold and other debris.

Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean.
